newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SAIL to raise steel prices.
newsitem.headline: India's SAIL to raise steel prices.

text.p: State-run Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) plans to increase steel product prices from April 1 due to rising input costs and a railway freight rate hike, the United News of India (UNI) said on Sunday.

The news agency quoted a SAIL spokesman as saying the firm would bear an additional cost of 10 billion rupees ($279.33 million) in 1996/97 (April-March) due to a rise in the costs of coal, petroleum and power.
Prices of coking coal have surged by 27 to 38 percent over the last six months and prices of petroleum products have risen by 15 to 30 percent, the spokesman said.

UNI quoted the spokesman as saying a hike in input transportation costs would burden the steel maker with an additional cost of 1.8 billion rupees and also increase outward freight on SAIL's finished steel.
It did not say how much SAIL planned to raise prices by.
India last month proposed a 12 percent increase in freight charges for most goods.
Based on the existing average railway freight of 1,000 rupees per tonne of saleable steel, the additional cost of outward freight for SAIL works out at 1.3 billion rupees, the news agency said.

SAIL normally adjusts its prices twice a year, in January and July. The company did not raise prices in January due to a sluggish market but the recent freight hike could not be absorbed by the company, the spokesman said. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
